newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian police round up 130 illegal immigrants.
newsitem.headline: Italian police round up 130 illegal immigrants.

text.p: Police rounded up 130 people from Sri Lanka and Pakistan on Friday as the latest wave of illegal immigration hit Italy's southern coast.
Twenty people were picked up on a beach near the city of Reggio Calabria where they had landed on dinghies while the others were apprehended on a Honduras-flagged ship.
The would-be immigrants, some of whom were suffering from the early stages of frostbite, would be served with expulsion orders, police said.
However, authorities acknowledge many illegal immigrants ignore the noticies and stay in Italy or try to move on to other European countries.
The shores of southern Italy and a remote island between Sicily and North Africa, Lampedusa, are favoured entry points for would-be immigrants to Italy.
On Monday, police rounded up 125 people who tried to enter southern parts of the country illegally by boat.

Seventy-four -- from Albania, Turkey, Montenegro and Egypt -- were stopped along the coast of Puglia, across the Adriatic from Albania. Most of the others were North Africans stopped on the small island of Pantelleria, between Sicily and Tunisia.
